newsitem.title: CHINA: Hong Kong gold ends down on overseas sales.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends down on overseas sales.

text.p: Hong Kong spot gold ended a shade down on Friday from New York's previous close after a spurt of afternoon selling from Europe erased the morning's solid gains, dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$323.30/80 per ounce compared to New York's close at US$323.50/324.00 on Thursday.
"We were sitting at $323.50 and it was next trading nearer $323.00," said one dealer.
Compared to the day's high of $325.50/326.00, the selling around Asia's closing time meant some punters got burned, dealers said.
"This morning was looking so good and then it just came off in very choppy trade," another source said.
Traders saw support at $322.50 per ounce and said they expected to see another bout of shortcovering.
Physical demand had quietened in the wake of higher prices, traders said.
Local tael gold ended HK$44 higher at HK$2,996.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society rose to +2.00 from its previous fix at nil.
